title: Treesa-Gayatri Clinch Historic World Championships Bronze
indian_angle: This marks India's continued success in women's doubles and ends a 15-year drought for an Indian women's doubles medal at the World Championships.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a bronze medal at the BWF World Championships after their impressive run ended in the semi-finals against top seeds Sheng and Ning. Their achievement is India's first women's doubles medal in 15 years, echoing the success of Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa in 2011.

title: Gopichand Outlines India's Asian Games Strategy Post-Worlds
indian_angle: National coach Pullela Gopichand's plans for the upcoming Asian Games are crucial for India's medal prospects following the World Championships.
summary: National coach Pullela Gopichand shared India's strategic approach for the upcoming Asian Games, emphasizing focused training after the BWF World Championships. This comes as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a bronze medal, providing momentum for the team.

title: Satwik-Chirag Bow Out of Worlds in Quarter-Finals
indian_angle: India's top men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, faced an early exit from the World Championships, raising concerns about their fitness.
summary: India's star men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, were defeated by China's Chang and Liang in the BWF World Championships quarter-finals with a score of 21-18, 21-9, ending their campaign amidst fitness concerns.

title: BAI Praised for Successful World Championships Hosting
indian_angle: The Badminton Association of India successfully hosted the BWF World Championships in India, demonstrating enhanced organizational capabilities after 17 years.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) has received commendation for successfully hosting the BWF World Championships in India after a 17-year gap. The organization improved facilities based on feedback from the India Open, showcasing a significant step forward in managing major international events.

title: Indian Junior Team Coaching Camp Underway in Guwahati
indian_angle: This coaching camp is vital for preparing India's young talent for the upcoming Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships.
summary: A national coaching camp for the Indian team participating in the Badminton Asia U17 & U15 Junior Championships 2026 is currently being held at the National Center of Excellence in Guwahati, focusing on developing the next generation of Indian badminton stars.

title: New 3x15 Scoring System for Junior Domestic Tournaments
indian_angle: The implementation of the 3x15 scoring system in domestic junior tournaments will impact how young Indian players compete and develop.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has announced the implementation of a 3x15 scoring system for domestic ranking tournaments and National Championships across the U-13, U-15, and U-17 age groups, aiming to standardize play for junior categories.
